text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Retailer Vendex Int.'s services group Vedior to be listed on Amsterdam and London stock exchanges in early June. (p1)
- Textile producer Vlisco's cloth worth gold in Zaire. (p1)
- Former chairman of Nedcar takes helm at public transport group VSN. (p3)
- New retail combination De Boer/Unigro to close head office and four of its nine distribution centres. (p3)
- Dairy concern Campina Melkunie appoints new chief at its German subsidiary Campina AG. (p3)
- Joint venture of tuggers Smit Int. and Wijsmuller in alliance with South Africa's shipowner Safmarine. (p3)
- BE Semiconductor Industry BESI reports Q1 net plunges from Dfl 12.4 million to Dfl 4.1 million. (p5)
- Builder BAM's infrastructural and environmental activities grow turnover 30 pct independent of acquisitions. (p5)
VOLKSKRANT
- Pig farmers in province of Brabant to blame for spreading of swine fever. (p1)
- TV productions company IDTV forced to shed jobs due to declining orders. (p1)
- European council of finance ministers crosses the Netherlands off the list of countries with excessive budget deficits. (p2)
- Dutch PTT Telecom threatened with having to yield part of telecom frequencies to rival Libertel. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- The Dutch exporting sector criticises junior minister of foreign trade for pursuing bad policy. (p3)
- Ailing automation group Triple P on lookout for new capital. (27)
- Grand Hotel Krasnapolsky signs letter of intent with Israel's builder Alevy to build 311 room hotel in Israel. (p29)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Royal Dutch/Shell still lies and deceives too often, says critical report by Project Underground and Rainforest Action Network to be presented today. (p12)
TROUW
- Automation company CMG shows clearly better performance in first four months of 1997 compared to year-earlier period. (p14)
